newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end higher, outperforming U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end higher, outperforming U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds ended higher on Monday, outperforming their U.S. counterparts in light trading with most trading completed by midday, traders said.
They said Canadian bonds were up in the long end on the strength of early morning buying interest, but little trading activity occurred in the afternoon.
"It was pretty quiet, but we did outperform the U.S." one trader said.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.30 to C$112.50 to yield 6.958 percent, compared to a yield of 6.54 percent for the U.S. 30-year which dropped 2/32 to 99.14/32 on the day.
Without much economic or even corporate news, bond traders had little to hang their hats on and many of their clients remain out of the market as they wind up Christmas holidays.
"We've got about half the regular staff here," another trader said.
In scant economic news, the U.S. Conference Board index of leading, coincident and lagging indicators rose 0.1 percent in November after being unchanged in October.
In the middle of the yield curve Canada's 10-year bond rose C$0.28 to C$105.28 to yield 6.275 percent, while Canada's two-year was up C$0.06 to C$103.76 to yield 3.939 percent.
